paper_metadata.title: Effect of nitrogen on the microstructure evolution and mechanical properties of Ni-Fe base superalloys during long-term thermal exposure

evidence.quote: Effect of nitrogen on the microstructure evolution and mechanical properties of Ni-Fe base superalloys during long-term thermal exposure

Two newly-developed Ni – Fe base superalloys were investigated in this study. The chemical composition (wt%) of two alloys are 42.0 Fe, 15.0 Cr, 1.6 W + Mo + Co, 3.6 Ti + Al, 0.04 C, 0.003 B, 0.0011 N with the balance Ni (GH4070R(HT700R)), and 30.0 Fe, 20.0 Cr, 1.0 W + Mo + Co, 3.8 Ti + Al, 0.05 C, 0.002 B, 0.0015 N with the balance Ni (GH4650T (HT650T)), designated as A1 and A2 in this study, respectively.

attributes.composition: core enriched in Ti and N; shell enriched in W and C

evidence.quote: The core-shell structure of the M(C, N) was observed, in which the core is enriched of Ti and N and the shell of W and C. The M(C, N) phase was stable without obvious decomposition during the thermal exposure.
M23C6 was found to maintain the discrete distribution at the grain boundary even under the thermal exposure at 700 ◦C for 7004 h.
Addition of N leads to the formation of Ti(C, N) phase at GBs, which can suppress the formation of continuous M23C6 carbides at GBs during the long term thermal exposure at 700 ◦C.

The suppression of γ’ coarsening can be attributed to the consumption of γ’-forming element Ti by formation of more stable M(C, N) phase during thermal exposure when N was added in the Ni-Fe alloys.
